newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs called lower in west, firm in east.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs called lower in west, firm in east.

text.p: Cash hogs were called steady to lower in Iowa and Illinois direct markets and steady to firm in Indiana and Ohio markets on Wednesday, cash dealers said.
Lower cash pork prices at midday Tuesday coupled with packers buying enough hogs to satisfy much of Wednesday's slaughter should weigh on hog prices then, they said.
Also, forecasts for warm, clear weather Wednesday should encourage marketings, they said. Spring planting was largely finished and producers have time to market hogs.
Iowa/Minnesota sources expect hog prices at $55.00 to $55.50 per cwt at country points and $56.50 at plants.
Iowa and Illinois dealers said meat packers have negative operating margins which may worsen following the latest decline in pork prices.
USDA at midday Tuesday quoted cash pork bellies down $5.00 to $6.00 per cwt, trimmings down $1.00 to $5.00, hams steady to $1.00 lower and loins weak.

Indiana and Ohio sources said active fieldwork may keep hog marketings light and support prices. Warm, dry weather this week had farmers actively planting soybeans and doing other fieldwork, which had been delayed by abundant rain there in recent weeks.
